method: Ninth clause checked this session, top of the classification-aware authority queue (verification/classification/proposals.json's 45-clause authority set, cross-referenced against verification/findings/ to find the 37 still unchecked -- the raw npm run queue output mixes drafting and authority clauses because queue.mjs does not read proposals.json, so it is not a reliable ordering for this ladder). The clause makes three separable factual claims -- a completion deadline, a retention rule, and a nondiscrimination/documentary-uniformity rule -- backed by a single citation to 8 U.S.C. section 1324a. Checked each claim independently rather than treating the citation as covering all three. Per the user's instruction to double every check, went back for a second, independent circuit's opinion after the first pass rather than stopping at Robison alone -- Split Rail Fence Co. v. United States (10th Cir. 2017), a different circuit and 19 years later, closed two things the first pass had left open: it quotes the regulation's three-business-day text directly, and it quotes the current post-1996 text of section 1324b(a)(6), which Robison had only described secondhand.

assertions.text: applying the same documentary requirements to all employees, without regard to national origin or citizenship status, is what the law requires
assertions.note: Robison Fruit Ranch, Inc. v. United States, 154 F.3d 807 (9th Cir. 1998), and Split Rail Fence Co. v. United States, 852 F.3d 1228 (10th Cir. 2017), both quoted below. This claim is not actually a section 1324a claim -- it is the 'document abuse' provision, 8 U.S.C. section 1324b(a)(6), read together with the general antidiscrimination provision, section 1324b(a)(1). The clause's single citation names only section 1324a, the verification-duty statute, and omits section 1324b, the antidiscrimination statute that is the actual source of this specific claim -- a miscitation in the sense this project's taxonomy uses the term, even though the underlying legal claim itself holds up. Robison (9th Cir.) held that requesting more or different documents from some employees than others is unlawful only where done for a discriminatory purpose or with discriminatory effect; treating everyone identically, which is what the clause instructs, is the safe-harbor practice the statute is designed to induce. Split Rail (10th Cir., 19 years later) independently quotes the current statutory text of section 1324b(a)(6) -- 'shall be treated as an unfair immigration-related employment practice if made for the purpose or with the intent of discriminating against an individual' -- confirming Robison's account of the 1996 amendment from a second, independent circuit rather than taking Robison's own description of the amendment on faith.

assertions.text: Form I-9 must be completed within three (3) business days of the employee's first day of work
assertions.note: Split Rail Fence Co. v. United States, 852 F.3d 1228 (10th Cir. 2017), quoted below, directly quotes 8 C.F.R. section 274a.2(b)(1)(ii): an employer 'must within three business days of hire ... [c]omplete [S]ection 2' of Form I-9. Found by a full-text search inside the opinion (search_document, query 'business days') after the first-pass CourtListener searches for this claim came back empty -- the claim was there in a case already in the corpus, it just was not the headline holding of any opinion returned by a topic search, and needed a targeted in-document search to surface. This upgrades the assertion from the earlier unsupported finding: a court's own quotation of the regulatory text is exactly the kind of corroboration this project treats as real, even though the host is still courtlistener.com (mirror tier) rather than the regulation's own publisher host, which remains blocked.

assertions.text: I-9 forms must be retained separately from personnel files
assertions.note: Full-text searches inside both Robison and Split Rail (queries 'retain', 'personnel') found no discussion of this specific sub-requirement -- Split Rail's retention discussion concerns keeping photocopies of examined documents with the I-9 form itself, not the separate question of where the I-9 form is filed relative to the rest of the personnel file. This remains a regulatory recordkeeping detail (8 C.F.R. section 274a.2(b)(2) region) with no case law found addressing it directly. eCFR and the other hosts that would carry the regulation directly remain blocked (re-probed 2026-08-21, unchanged).

gaps: The clause's citation (8 U.S.C. section 1324a only) does not name section 1324b, which is the actual statutory source of the documentary-uniformity claim. Whether this is worth flagging as a citation gap depends on whether a reader would understand '8 U.S.C. section 1324a' to cover the whole clause or just the verification-duty sentence -- not resolved here, but noted because this project's stated failure pattern is exactly 'the clause reproduces something true and cites the wrong or incomplete provision.'

The retain-separately-from-personnel-files claim is still unsupported after two independent cases and targeted in-document searches of both -- not for lack of trying, but because no litigated dispute this search surfaced has turned on that specific sub-requirement.

judicialQuotations.case: Robison Fruit Ranch, Inc. v. United States (9th Cir. 1998) 154 F.3d 807
judicialQuotations.quote: We hold that Congress intended a discrimination requirement in the 1990 statute and merely clarified the statute to state that intent in its 1996 amendment. The evidence unquestionably shows that the employment practices in this case did not create additional burdens to any class of applicants or constitute differential treatment of authorized aliens and citizens. There could have been no discrimination, and the petition for review must be granted.

judicialQuotations.case: Robison Fruit Ranch, Inc. v. United States (9th Cir. 1998) 154 F.3d 807
judicialQuotations.quote: The ALJ in Zabala concluded that a request for specific documents did not violate section 1324b(a)(6) when the employer requested documents that are in fact routinely presented during the employment process... Inferring a discrimination requirement from the language of the statute, that ALJ held that section 1324b(a)(6) 'is not breached in the absence of evidence that ... aliens but not other new hires were required to rely on and produce specific documents.' We agree.

judicialQuotations.case: Split Rail Fence Co. v. United States (10th Cir. 2017) 852 F.3d 1228
judicialQuotations.quote: The employer must complete Section 2, titled "Employer Review and Verification," to confirm the identity and employment authorization of the employee by listing the document numbers and expiration dates of examined documents. See id. § 274a.2(b)(1)(ii) (explaining an employer "must within three business days of hire ... [c]omplete [S]ection 2").

judicialQuotations.case: Split Rail Fence Co. v. United States (10th Cir. 2017) 852 F.3d 1228
judicialQuotations.quote: ...documents than are required under such section or refusing to honor documents tendered that on their face reasonably appear to be genuine shall be treated as an unfair immigration-related employment practice if made for the purpose or with the intent of discriminating against an individual." 8 U.S.C. § 1324b(a)(6).
